title: rorca-codebase-audit

userStories.title: Zod Request Validation on All POST/PUT/PATCH Endpoints
userStories.description: SOTA TypeScript/Express backends validate every incoming mutation at the boundary with Zod schemas. Currently most route handlers in backend/src/routes/ parse req.body.field directly with no schema validation — trusting callers to send correct shapes. This is a security and reliability gap. Add Zod schemas for every POST, PUT, and PATCH endpoint's request body. Validation middleware should throw ValidationError(400) with field-level detail on schema mismatch. Pattern: define a Zod schema per endpoint, call .parse(req.body) or .safeParse() before any business logic, throw new ValidationError(details) on failure. The existing AppError infrastructure (CA-002–004) makes this clean.
acceptanceCriteria: New backend/src/lib/validate.ts exports a validateBody<T>(schema: ZodSchema<T>) Express middleware factory
validateBody wraps schema.parse(req.body), catches ZodError, and throws ValidationError(400) with { field, message } details per failed field
Every POST endpoint in backend/src/routes/ uses validateBody middleware before the route handler
Every PUT and PATCH endpoint in backend/src/routes/ uses validateBody middleware
GET and DELETE endpoints validate URL params and query strings with a validateParams/validateQuery middleware
ValidationError responses include a details array: [{ field: 'email', message: 'Invalid email format' }]
Zod schemas co-located with route handlers (not a separate schema file) — one schema per endpoint for discoverability
cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit passes — all Zod inferred types propagate correctly
cd backend && npm test passes — existing tests updated to send valid payloads
grep -rn 'req.body\.' backend/src/routes/ | wc -l is ≤ 10 (only remaining uses are inside validated handlers accessing already-parsed fields via res.locals or typed req)

userStories.title: OpenAPI @swagger Annotation Completeness Audit
userStories.description: Rorca's architecture is API-first: the OpenAPI spec auto-generated from @swagger JSDoc annotations is the source of truth for REST, MCP tools, and the VS Code extension. Currently many routes have missing or incomplete annotations (no requestBody schema, missing response schemas, no error response docs). This story audits every route in backend/src/routes/ and adds missing @swagger annotations so the generated OpenAPI spec at GET /api/docs/openapi.json is complete. A complete annotation includes: summary, description, tags, requestBody schema (for mutation endpoints), response 200 schema, response 400/401/404/500 schemas. This unblocks the planned MCP Streamable HTTP transport (CA-021 from convention-agents spec) which auto-generates MCP tools FROM the OpenAPI spec.
acceptanceCriteria: Every route handler in backend/src/routes/ has a @swagger JSDoc block
Every route has: summary, description, tags, at least one 2xx response schema
Every POST/PUT/PATCH route has requestBody with application/json schema
Every route that can fail has 400, 401, 404 response schemas documented
GET /api/docs/openapi.json returns a valid OpenAPI 3.0 spec with zero missing schemas
Swagger UI at GET /api/docs renders all routes with full parameter and response docs
No 'unknown' or 'any' types in generated OpenAPI schemas — all properties typed
Tags are consistent: 'Specs', 'Pipeline', 'Workspaces', 'Direction', 'Analytics', 'Auth', 'Skills', 'Teams', 'Billing', 'Integrations'
swagger-jsdoc generates without warnings: npx swagger-jsdoc -d swaggerDef.ts 'backend/src/routes/**/*.ts' exits 0
AGENTS.md updated with OpenAPI annotation guidelines and required fields checklist
